headline: A 2021 law sets confidentiality rules for peer support counseling given to law enforcement officers and directs the Justice Department to create best practices for these programs.
what_it_does: The law covers counseling programs that police and other law enforcement agencies provide, in which a peer support specialist counsels an officer in the agency. It generally bars disclosing the contents of a peer support communication. It also requires the Department of Justice to develop best practices and professional standards for these programs.

who_it_affects.how: Communications with a peer support specialist are generally protected from disclosure under the law.

who_it_affects.group: Law enforcement agencies that run peer support counseling programs
who_it_affects.how: They must follow confidentiality rules for these programs and may use the Justice Department's future best practices and standards.
They are subject to the law's confidentiality requirements when counseling officers.
It must develop best practices and professional standards for peer support counseling programs.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 18, 2021; the summary does not state a separate effective date.
